videos.title: Static and Dynamic Equilibrium: Equal Rates, Not Equal Amounts | Year 12 Chemistry
videos.description:
Distinguish static equilibrium, dynamic equilibrium and systems that are still changing. Use a sealed sparkling drink, a salt jar and equal traffic between two towns to explain why equal opposing rates do not mean equal amounts. Practise classifying three everyday cases.

Chemistry 2017: Year 12 Module 5, Equilibrium and Acid Reactions. Supports static and dynamic equilibrium and the differences between open and closed systems.
Syllabus dotpoint (NSW Chemistry Stage 6, 2017, Module 5):
"model static and dynamic equilibrium and analyse the differences between open and closed systems"
Official 2017 course: https://www.nsw.gov.au/education-and-training/nesa/curriculum/science/chemistry-stage-6-2017

Prerequisite: Reversible reactions, moving particles and reaction rate. Next: How reaction rates change on the way to equilibrium.

videos.title: Sexual and Asexual Reproduction: Continuity and Variation | Year 12 Biology
videos.description:
Explain how passing on DNA and producing offspring that survive to reproduce keep a species going. Compare sexual and asexual reproduction by variation, speed, partners and energy, then use changing conditions to judge which method helps. The Cavendish banana and TR4 disease show why shared DNA can become a shared weakness.

Biology 2017: Year 12 Module 5, Heredity. Supports sexual and asexual mechanisms of reproduction and continuity of a species.
Syllabus dotpoint (NSW Biology Stage 6, 2017, Module 5):
"explain the mechanisms of reproduction that ensure the continuity of a species, by analysing sexual and asexual methods of reproduction in a variety of organisms"
Official 2017 course: https://www.nsw.gov.au/education-and-training/nesa/curriculum/science/biology-stage-6-2017

Prerequisite: Cells contain DNA that carries inherited information. Next: How animals bring sperm and egg together.

#Year12Biology #Reproduction #HSCScience

videos.title: How Bread Mould Spreads: Spores and New Growth | Year 12 Biology
videos.description:
Follow how bread mould releases spores that travel through the air and start new fungal growth when conditions are suitable. Identify fungal threads and spore cases, then explain how mould can reach a second piece of bread without the pieces touching. Connect this spore-making route to asexual reproduction.

Biology 2017: Year 12 Module 5, Heredity. Supports fungal reproduction through spores.

Syllabus dotpoint (NSW Biology Stage 6, 2017, Module 5):
"explain the mechanisms of reproduction that ensure the continuity of a species, by analysing sexual and asexual methods of reproduction in a variety of organisms, including but not limited to:
- fungi: budding, spores"
Official 2017 course: https://www.nsw.gov.au/education-and-training/nesa/curriculum/science/biology-stage-6-2017

Prerequisite: Sexual and asexual reproduction and continuity of a species. Next: How yeast reproduces by budding.

#Year12Biology #Fungi #HSCScience
